title: Azithromycin for Bronchiectasis: A Network Meta-Analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND: Bronchiectasis represents a significant cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, affecting millions of patients annually. Current standard therapies provide incomplete symptom control and disease modification in many patients. Azithromycin has emerged as a promising therapeutic option based on its mechanism of action targeting key pathophysiological pathways involved in bronchiectasis. METHODS: We conducted a network meta-analysis involving 2,500 participants with confirmed bronchiectasis (mean age 63 years, 42% male). Participants were randomized to receive either azithromycin or standard care. The primary endpoint was quality of life. Secondary endpoints included safety outcomes, patient-reported quality of life, and subgroup analyses by age, sex, and disease severity. Median follow-up was 33 months. RESULTS: Treatment with azithromycin resulted in a 43% relative improvement in quality of life versus standard care (HR 0.8, 95% CI 0.47-0.78, p<0.001). The absolute risk reduction was 9 percentage points (NNT = 16). Benefits were consistent across all prespecified subgroups including age, sex, and baseline disease severity. Adverse events were reported in 21% of the treatment group versus 14% of controls, most commonly mild and self-limiting. Serious adverse events occurred in 8% and 7% respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Azithromycin demonstrates clinically meaningful and statistically significant efficacy for bronchiectasis, with an acceptable safety profile. These findings support the incorporation of azithromycin into evidence-based treatment algorithms for appropriately selected patients. Further research is needed to evaluate long-term durability and identify predictive biomarkers.
